messages:
Maya (CSE): Quick heads-up — Fluxly onboarding: their frontend SDK init is getting intermittent 429s right after ephemeral token rotation. Started ~17:02 UTC. Customer says it looks like a token churn + preflight fanout pattern.

Maya (CSE): Example log lines they pasted: `2026-03-23T17:02:14Z GET /v1/embeddings 429 rate_limit tenant=fluxly request_id=abc123` then `2026-03-23T17:02:15Z token refresh success new_token_id=tkn_9f3e` then more 429s. Looks like lots of parallel inits that coincide with refreshes.

Jorge (Eng): Thanks — do we know what SDK + version and whether they're using prefetch/prefetchConcurrency? Also, any x-request-id or client_nano info?

Maya (CSE): They're on browser-sdk 1.3.2. Client is initializing per-tab and calling embed() on mount, no explicit splaying. Sample init code they sent: ```js
// app init (simplified)
const token = await fetch('/.auth/ephemeral');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: token });
client.embed({ model: 'rwd-embed-1' }).then(...);
// multiple tabs/users spawn this in parallel
```

Sam (Platform): This matches a classic ephemeral token fanout. If token TTL is short and many inits race, we see ~N preflight calls all hitting rate windows. Short-term mitigations: set client-side splay/backoff on init, and throttle fetches (maxParallelFetches=2). Server-side: increase ephemeral token grace window and enable short-lived tenant burst allowance.

Jorge (Eng): Can you paste a raw request header with the SDK metadata? Need to confirm `x-rwd-client` and `x-rwd-init` fields. Also, any recent deploys that might have changed token TTL logic? @deploy-bot any config changes in the last 24h affecting token TTL?

Maya (CSE): Pasted one header: `x-rwd-client: browser-js/1.3.2`, `x-rwd-init: true`, `user-agent: Fluxly/1.0`.

deploy-bot: Config change deployed 2026-03-23T12:50:22Z: reduced ephemeral token grace from 10s -> 3s for tighter security testing (owner: infra/token-service).

Sam (Platform): Aha — that shrink could absolutely expose races. Recommend reverting grace to 10s for hosted onboarding tenants or adding a temporary grace override for fluxly. Ops can add a tenant-level exception while customer rolls out splay.

Maya (CSE): I'm going to ask Fluxly to apply a quick client-side patch to serialize init calls (small snippet) and will apply a feature flag on their env. Meanwhile can ops add a short-lived scope bump? @ops-oncall can you help?

ops-oncall: On it. I'll patch the tenant quota window and add a temporary token-grace override for tenant=fluxly for 45 minutes. Will also watch token-service logs.

Jorge (Eng): Also suggest pushing a small SDK patch in 1.3.x to add a default init splay for browser environments (100-400ms random) and limit concurrent preflight fetches. I'll open an issue and a tiny PR.

Maya (CSE): Customer applied the splay in a patched build and saw immediate reduction in 429s in our staging window. They reported 17:08 UTC: "init errors dropped to near zero".

ops-oncall: Temporary override applied at 17:10 UTC. Observed preflight fanout drop and token-service returned to expected latencies. I'll remove override at 17:55 unless you ask to extend.

Sam (Platform): Follow-ups: 1) revert the token grace reduction in canary until we validate splay rollout; 2) add an onboarding KB article (playbook) covering ephemeral token fanout + recommended client settings; 3) add a short-term metric on concurrent init spikes to alert CSE.

Maya (CSE): I'll write the KB draft and send to eng for review. Also scheduling a 30m postmortem/demo with Fluxly tomorrow to confirm renewal health — want to show we mitigated.

Jorge (Eng): Filed issue #ENG-4821: "browser-sdk: default init splay + maxParallelFetches" and linked PR for 1.3.x.

Maya (CSE): Closing loop with customer: they confirmed fix in prod later today. They're happy with mitigation and asked for docs. Thanks team! :raised_hands:

ops-oncall: Removing override at 17:55 UTC now. Will reopen if any regressions show up. :white_check_mark:

Maya (CSE): Will follow up tomorrow AM with account health note and renewal check-in.
